Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 21-Dec-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Nanotechnology and Applications [PHY_4345]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Assess the formation of energy bands in solids using the concept of overlapping atomic orbitals.       (5)  
  
  
  A)                                                       Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Explain the electrical properties of nano materials                                                    (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)           Relate why the optical properties of quantum dots are size-dependent?                                  (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Identify the principle of lithography? mention the types of nanolithography. Explain photo             (5)  
  nanolithography with neat diagram.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Explain with suitable examples how Solvothermal synthesis can be tuned to control nanomaterial         (3)  
  morphology.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)           Identify which method is suitable for preparing quantum dots and state the reason for your choice.     (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                Find how Bragg's Law is applied in determining the crystal structure of an unknown sample using X- (5)  
  ray diffraction (XRD) with neat diagram  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Apply the working principle of EDAX/EDS to explain how purity of the samples can be found for          (3)  
  prepared nano materials.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Identify how Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) can be used to measure surface roughness at the             (2)  
  nanoscale.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  Page #1

4)                        Apply your understanding of nanocomposite structures to assess how adding graphene sheets to a (5)  
  polymer matrix improves its mechanical and electrical performance. Support your answer with  
  A)                examples of practical applications  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)                Use the concept of fullerene structure to predict how changing the size (number of carbon atoms)         (5)  
  affects its electronic and chemical properties.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)                        Illustrate working principle of hybrid solar cells to design an energy-harvesting system for wearable    (5)  
  electronic devices.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)                Use your knowledge of nano-sensors to propose how they could be applied in medical diagnostics           (5)  
  for early disease detection.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  -----End-----
